---
title: "Step 2 — Install the packages"
subtitle: "Step 2 of 5"
---

**Time:** 20 minutes, mostly waiting.
**Before you start:** [Step 1](install.qmd) finished, and RStudio open.
**When you finish:** 12 packages installed, and a check that says your laptop
is ready.

There are no files to download. Both lines below run straight from this site.

## Step 1 of 3 — Install the packages

1. Open RStudio.
2. Click once inside the **Console** pane, at the bottom left.
3. Copy the line below. Paste it into the Console. Press **Enter**.

```r
source("https://drarunmitra.github.io/iisc-epi-shortcourse/setup/install_packages.R")
```

4. Leave the computer alone until it finishes.

**You should see:** lines of text scrolling past, naming each package as it
installs. This takes 10 to 25 minutes the first time. You are finished when the
`>` prompt comes back and stops moving.

**If it does not work:** if R asks
`Do you want to install from sources the package which needs compilation?`,
type `n` and press **Enter**.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not interrupt it
Close RStudio part way through and some packages are left half-installed. The
line above installs only what is still missing, so run it again and let it
finish.

Red text in R is not always an error. Most of it is ordinary progress output.
:::

## Step 2 of 3 — Run the check

1. Click once inside the **Console** pane.
2. Copy the line below. Paste it into the Console. Press **Enter**.

```r
source("https://drarunmitra.github.io/iisc-epi-shortcourse/setup/check_setup.R")
```

**You should see:** about 8 lines, then this:

```
You are ready for 21 September. See you at IISc.
```

**If it does not work:** read the line that starts with a cross. It names the
fix. Then read [Troubleshooting](../resources/troubleshooting.qmd).

| Symbol | Means |
|---|---|
| ✔ | that check passed |
| ! | a warning; usually fine, read the text |
| ✖ | that check failed; fix this one |

## Step 3 of 3 — Email us if anything failed

Only if you saw a cross.

1. Select the whole check output in the Console and copy it.
2. Email it to
   [office.msicph@iisc.ac.in](mailto:office.msicph@iisc.ac.in).
3. Say which operating system you use, and its version.

**You should see:** the email in your Sent folder.

**If it does not work:** paste the output as text, not as a screenshot. We
cannot search a picture.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
R on its own does very little. Packages do the work. This course uses 12 of
them.

The check tests behaviour, not only what sits on disk. It runs `epitools` on a
2×2 table with a known answer. A broken install fails now, not in front of the
class.

Tell us about a failure early. A problem we see on Wednesday is a working
laptop by Friday.
:::
